trigger_condition: 'encrypted-in-transit claim set' describes in-memory data; transit encryption does not apply
guard_snippet: Say plaintext in process memory keyed by code hash, or specify the in-memory encryption key and its home
potential_consequence: False assurance carried into DPIA/RoPA aids

trigger_condition: Claims deleted at code exchange and personal_code barred from bearer tokens, so userinfo has no claim source
guard_snippet: Choose: claims embedded in signed access token, drop userinfo in v1, or a bounded per-token claim cache in the lifecycle table
potential_consequence: userinfo breaks or reintroduces server-side retention

trigger_condition: Addendum derives public sub from country+ID code; raw/reversible sub leaks the personal code to every client
guard_snippet: Both public and pairwise sub = HMAC(server secret, scope‖country‖code)
potential_consequence: National ID leaks via a mandatory claim; opt-in allow-list bypassed

trigger_condition: Rotating the pairwise secret changes every sub but is framed as routine
guard_snippet: Versioned pairwise key id; rotation is a migration event; back up with signing-key custody
potential_consequence: Every client's account links silently orphaned

location: Public surface (JWKS retention) + ADR-005 incident matrix
trigger_condition: Retention rule has no override for key compromise
guard_snippet: Compromised keys removed from JWKS immediately; drill covers emergency revocation
potential_consequence: Forged tokens verify during an incident

trigger_condition: private_key_jwt key source unspecified; jwks_uri fetch adds egress/SSRF
guard_snippet: Inline static client JWKS only; no jwks_uri in v1
potential_consequence: Breaks egress isolation (NFR-004), new SSRF vector

trigger_condition: acr_values, prompt, max_age, claims request params unspecified
guard_snippet: Unprovable acr_values → unmet_authentication_requirements; never silently downgrade
potential_consequence: Clients get lower assurance than requested

trigger_condition: Unauthenticated authorize creates flows; no overflow behavior, no code-store bound, no per-IP/client sub-quota
guard_snippet: 503 on overflow, separate code-store cap, per-IP/client quotas, lazy upstream session creation
potential_consequence: One bot denies login to all or burns RP upstream quota

trigger_condition: Polling model and global upstream concurrency undefined
guard_snippet: Server-side poller with global rate cap; cancel upstream on abandon
potential_consequence: Upstream rate limit/ban; all logins fail

trigger_condition: Web2App return lands in a different browser/webview; cookie attributes unspecified
guard_snippet: Define cross-browser return binding; __Host-, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax
potential_consequence: Mobile Web2App failures or weakened binding enabling takeover

trigger_condition: Missing real-time QR relay phishing and XSS/clickjacking rows
guard_snippet: Add QR-relay row (freshness, verification code, origin display, relay test) and UI row (CSP, frame-ancestors 'none', autoescape)
potential_consequence: Most practical eID takeover routes untested

trigger_condition: Demo/prod separation relies only on clients checking claims
guard_snippet: Distinct demo issuer and demo-labelled key; production rejects demo key fingerprints
potential_consequence: Lax client accepts demo identities

trigger_condition: Readiness fails on full capacity
guard_snippet: Readiness = config/key load only; saturation → per-request 503
potential_consequence: Load spike becomes total outage

trigger_condition: No graceful shutdown; deploys kill flows and unexchanged codes
guard_snippet: SIGTERM: stop new authorize, drain ≤ code TTL/grace, exit
potential_consequence: Every deploy causes login and token-exchange failures

trigger_condition: Omits browser→eidbridge front channel and eID app→Smart-ID leg; no trust boundaries
guard_snippet: Add U→O, app→scheme edges and trust-boundary groupings
potential_consequence: Threat model and proxy/egress config miss the public surface

trigger_condition: Mostly 'proposed' with no owner, trigger or date
guard_snippet: Decision table: ADR → status → Q-xx → owner → blocking FR → evidence
potential_consequence: Stories built on undecided architecture or blocked with no owner

trigger_condition: 'Build chooser after FR-005' contradicts 'no dead chooser UI'
guard_snippet: Only the registry contract test with a fake method until a demand trigger activates chooser+FR-019 together
potential_consequence: Premature UI/cookie scope, or gate ignored

trigger_condition: Init fails or user abandons before pending
guard_snippet: created→{pending|failed|cancelled}; pending→{…|cancelled}
potential_consequence: Non-terminal entries hold capacity

trigger_condition: COMPLETE with non-OK endResult
guard_snippet: Exhaustive endResult→state table; unknown → failed
potential_consequence: Unmapped code treated as success/undefined

trigger_condition: Retries exhausted while phone session still open
guard_snippet: Mark failed, never accept later result, tell user to cancel on device
potential_consequence: Phone shows success, browser login failed

trigger_condition: Store full while authorize requests arrive
guard_snippet: Reject with 503+Retry-After; never evict pending/verified
potential_consequence: Eviction flushing or unbounded memory

trigger_condition: Flow verifies while store is full
guard_snippet: Reserve code slot at flow creation or separate code cap
potential_consequence: Authenticated user gets no code

trigger_condition: In-flight poll returns verified after entry expired
guard_snippet: Missing/terminal entry → discard result, destroy secrets
potential_consequence: Flow resurrection or orphaned cert material

trigger_condition: Concurrent token requests with same code
guard_snippet: Atomic LoadAndDelete
potential_consequence: Two token sets per code

trigger_condition: Valid code with failed PKCE/client auth/redirect check
guard_snippet: Consume code on any failed exchange or cap attempts
potential_consequence: Verifier brute force or code burning

trigger_condition: Code replayed after token issuance
guard_snippet: Per-code jti deny-list for userinfo, or documented deviation
potential_consequence: OIDC replay-revocation rule unmet

trigger_condition: Refused/expired/failed or unexchanged code
guard_snippet: Clear cookies on every terminal state
potential_consequence: Stale cookie confuses next flow

trigger_condition: Two concurrent tabs
guard_snippet: Per-flow-handle cookie
potential_consequence: Second flow breaks the first

trigger_condition: Compromised key retained until token expiry
guard_snippet: Compromised → drop immediately
potential_consequence: Forged tokens validate

trigger_condition: Restart after rotation
guard_snippet: Persist retired public keys with not-after
potential_consequence: Pre-restart tokens fail verification

trigger_condition: Secret rotated or client switches sub mode
guard_snippet: Versioned secret, no in-place rotation; mode change needs migration
potential_consequence: All accounts unlinked

trigger_condition: Account identity ≠ requested identity
guard_snippet: → failed(identity_mismatch), no code
potential_consequence: Undefined state on substitution attempt

trigger_condition: Mode unset, or demo mode with production endpoints/credentials
guard_snippet: No default mode; demo rejects production host/pins/CA/UUID
potential_consequence: Real identities under acr=demo or unsafe default

trigger_condition: Set in production
guard_snippet: Require second acknowledgement flag or fail startup
potential_consequence: Unpinned production with only a log warning

trigger_condition: Proxy not configured as trusted hop
guard_snippet: Startup warning when all peers are private/LB addresses
potential_consequence: Per-IP limit throttles everyone

trigger_condition: Store full on single replica
guard_snippet: Readiness ignores transient capacity
potential_consequence: LB drops only replica

trigger_condition: Browser returns with lost flow handle
guard_snippet: Stable error page / error=access_denied to client redirect
potential_consequence: User stranded, client waits

trigger_condition: Wall-clock jump
guard_snippet: Monotonic clock for TTLs
potential_consequence: Codes expire early or outlive 60s

trigger_condition: Both keys active, client alg unspecified
guard_snippet: Per-client id_token_signed_response_alg, default RS256
potential_consequence: Client cannot verify tokens

trigger_condition: Remembered method removed
guard_snippet: Ignore cookie if method not in registry
potential_consequence: Flow errors on missing method

original: §Deferred adjacent wallet requirements and handoffs, whole section (427 words, 18% of the document)
revised: MOVE the ADJ table and the ADJ-17 paragraph to `source-reconciliation.md`, which already owns the ADJ IDs. Keep a two-sentence pointer: "Deferred adjacent wallet candidates (ADJ-01…ADJ-18) and out-of-product items are tracked in [source reconciliation](source-reconciliation.md). None are initial-release promises."
rationale: Scope violation. The section's own lead says these are "not new initial release promises", yet it is the largest section and sits ahead of the in-scope threat model. Saves about 395 words. Humans lose nothing because the table survives in its home document.

original: §Threat and validation model (179 words), placed last after deferred material
revised: MOVE to directly after §Public surface and identity contract, before ADR-001. If the deferred section is moved out, it can follow ADR-006 instead.
rationale: Buried critical information. The threat-to-control-to-evidence table is the most scannable statement of what the ADRs protect against, and it now sits behind 427 words of out-of-scope candidates. Readers get the "why" before the ADR "how". 0 words.

original: Document opening: §Status and authority (68 words) leads with caveats, and no section lists the decisions
revised: QUESTION: add a decision index under the H1, a six-row table with ADR, one-line decision and status (proposed gate / retained default / retained guardrail / proposed choice / accepted criterion / deferred), plus a line for open gates Q-01–Q-05.
rationale: The pyramid model wants the conclusion first. Statuses now appear only inside each ADR body, so readers must read all six to learn what is decided. Adds about 60 words.

original: §Status and authority: "Go single binary, standard-library-first dependencies and dual MIT/Apache-2.0 licensing are source constraints; choose exact runtime/library versions…"
revised: MOVE the constraints to the top of §Context and boundaries as a short "Constraints" list (Go single binary; stdlib-first; MIT/Apache-2.0; versions chosen at implementation). Keep only document status and authority in §Status.
rationale: Hard constraints sit inside a paragraph about the document's provenance. Separating them makes them scannable. About 0 words.

original: §Public surface and identity contract (274 words): RS256/JWKS rotation, pairwise subject, and the assurance/acr rule (paragraphs at lines 38–42)
revised: QUESTION: either number this section as an ADR (for example "ADR-000: OIDC public contract") with a Status line, or split the assurance paragraph into its own ADR.
rationale: The section holds decisions as consequential as the numbered ADRs, including signing algorithm, subject privacy and assurance claims, but it has no status. The document marks the pairwise default as "proposed… to confirm" only inline. That is inconsistent scaffolding for a decision record. 0 words (+5 for the Status line).

original: ADR-001 to ADR-006: free prose with a "Status:" lead only
revised: CONDENSE into a consistent schema, using bold lead-ins rather than new headings: **Status**, **Decision**, **Source reconciliation**, **Open gates/evidence**.
rationale: Each ADR mixes decision, source history and gating in different orders. ADR-001, for example, opens with the decision, and its second paragraph is source history. A consistent schema supports the random access readers use when they come back to one ADR. About +20 words.

original: ADR-005, paragraphs 3–4: "Operator docs require field/purpose/…" and "Production checklist: own RP agreement/…" (about 145 words)
revised: MOVE to the PRD's operations/documentation requirements or a future operator runbook. In ADR-005, leave one sentence: "Operator documentation and the production checklist are release-gating evidence; see [PRD §…]."
rationale: Scope violation. These are deliverable content requirements, not architecture decisions, and they make ADR-005 the most overloaded ADR (five concerns: artifacts, conformance table, operator docs, checklist/incidents, nightly workflow/support). Saves about 125 words. If they stay, convert the checklist to a bulleted list (see the pacing row).

original: ADR-006 "Wallet FR-022/023" paragraph: "SD-JWT/KB-JWT and mdoc require issuer/holder/audience/nonce/transcript binding…"
revised: MERGE with the ADJ-14 row, which says the same thing (issuer, holder, status, audience, nonce, transcript). Keep the prerequisites sentence and the conformance-harness sentence in ADR-006.
rationale: True redundancy: the same binding list is stated twice, three paragraphs apart. Saves about 40 words.

original: ADR-001: "MID/Web eID are not automatic low-cost substitutes; Web eID alone is estimated 80–100 hours and needs hardware/security review."
revised: CONDENSE to "MID/Web eID are not automatic low-cost substitutes (see ADR-006)."
rationale: Duplicates ADR-006's "80–100h… no 'cheap fallback' assumption". One source of truth for the estimate. Saves about 15 words.

original: ADR-001: "No fictional successful spike ADR is written by this planning task." · ADR-005: "This task records its acceptance requirement; it does not enable a cron, send messages or deploy an autonomous monitor."
revised: CUT both, or CONDENSE the second to "Acceptance requirement only; implementation needs separate authorization."
rationale: Process notes about the planning session, not the architecture. They will read as noise once the document outlives the task. Saves about 30 words.

original: Closing paragraph: "Apply actual implementation-specific security review before a production release. Planning/source coverage is not cryptographic review…" (27 words)
revised: MERGE into §Status and authority, next to "not an implementation survey".
rationale: Repeats the opening disclaimer. A single caveat at the top is enough, and the threat table then ends cleanly. Saves about 15 words net.

original: ADR-002 (303 words, five concerns: flow/code lifecycle, token lifecycle, persistence/HA, access logs, telemetry/egress)
revised: CONDENSE the lifecycle rules (lines 52–54) into a table with Data item / Created / Destroyed at / Notes (flow entry, challenge/cert secrets, claim set, auth code, access token, cookies). Add bold lead-ins "Persistence", "Logging" and "Egress" for the rest.
rationale: The lifecycle is sequential data that is hard to track in prose. A table is a visual aid that lets readers check each item's end of life, and it also makes the #10/#13 reconciliation visible. Saves about 40 words.

original: §Proposed layout (line 32): "cmd/eidbridge; internal/smartid; internal/authn and authntest; …"
revised: CONDENSE into a code-block tree or a bulleted list with a few words of responsibility per package.
rationale: Thirteen paths in a semicolon run-on cannot be scanned. A list improves pacing at about +15 words.

original: Pacing across the ADRs: dense paragraphs of 60–90 words built from slash-joined lists; ADR-005's "Maintain per-release table: requirement/profile version; implemented/deviation/not-run; …"
revised: QUESTION: render the per-release table as an empty table template, and put the production checklist and incident steps in bullet lists.
rationale: For human readers, the document has one diagram and two tables across about 2,300 words, with no whitespace inside sections. A table described in prose should be shown as a table. About 0 words.

original: Missing scaffolding: undefined terms (RP, MID, LoA, acr/amr, SPKI, LOTL/TL, HAIP, ARF, QTSP, QSCD, CSC, DPIA, RoPA, OIDF) and unlinked references (FR-xxx, Q-01–Q-05, issues #6/#8/#10/#13)
revised: QUESTION: link FR and Q IDs to the PRD and issue numbers to the tracker. Add a short glossary or link the PRD glossary.
rationale: The Microsoft Writing Style Guide asks you to spell out an acronym on first use unless your audience knows it. Readers new to eID cannot follow ADR-003 or ADR-006 without these definitions. About +80 to +100 words for a glossary, or about +10 for links only.

original: §Context and boundaries Mermaid diagram
revised: PRESERVE, and add a one-line lead-in such as "Request flow and trust inputs:".
rationale: This is the document's only visual aid and it anchors the mental model. Keep it. A lead-in helps screen-reader users and scanning, per Microsoft style. About +5 words.

original: Repeated status-check/Q-02 caveat (Public surface "Assurance", ADR-003 paragraph 3, threat table "explicit status policy")
revised: PRESERVE
rationale: Each mention applies the rule to a different surface (claims, certificate verification, trust drift). This is reinforcement, not redundancy.

original: "source" used alone as a noun throughout: "source constraints", "Source requests client_secret_basic…", "source default 10,000", "RS256 is source baseline", "source sketch LoA='high'", "the source prose loop", "per source", "Support source policy"
revised: Consider defining the term once in Status: "In this document, *source* means the GitHub issues and research inputs listed in the frontmatter."
rationale: Readers can take "source" to mean source code, which changes the meaning of "Source requests…" and "source default". One definition fixes every occurrence.

original: "Code/config receive production RP credentials from the operator."
revised: "The operator supplies production RP credentials through configuration; the code does not include them."
rationale: Says plainly who supplies the credentials and where they live. "Code/config receive" has no clear meaning.

original: "Operator keys persist across restart, old public keys remain in JWKS through issued token expiry and clock-skew allowance."
revised: "Operator keys persist across restarts. Old public keys remain in the JWKS until every issued token has expired, plus the clock-skew allowance."
rationale: Fixes the comma splice and makes the retention window readable.

original: "Upstream readiness diagnostics are opt-in/deferred under FR-026 and cannot make every health probe perform a network request."
revised: "Upstream readiness diagnostics are opt-in and deferred under FR-026, and they must not cause every health probe to make a network request."
rationale: "cannot" reads as a description of capability. "must not" states the requirement, which matches the modal verbs used elsewhere in the document.

original: "Assurance: never equate a method name, QUALIFIED certificate-level string or source sketch LoA='high' to legally established assurance automatically. Keep acr=demo in demo, publish evidence-backed production mapping and the selected policy/profile with status-check responsibilities (Q-02). Conflicting/unverified policy means do not assert the higher level."
revised: "Assurance: never automatically treat a method name, a `QUALIFIED` certificate level, or the source sketch's `LoA='high'` as legally established assurance. Keep `acr=demo` in demo mode. Publish an evidence-backed production mapping and the selected policy or profile, including who performs certificate status checks (Q-02). If the policy is conflicting or unverified, do not assert the higher level."
rationale: Moves "automatically" next to its verb, fixes the comma splice, and turns "means do not" into a clear condition.

original: "This removes the source prose loop 'chooser waits for second method' while MID depends on chooser."
revised: "This breaks the circular dependency in the source, where the chooser waits for a second method while Mobile-ID waits for the chooser."
rationale: "prose loop" is unclear. The revision names the cycle directly.

original: "Original spike says print subject fields and offers Mobile-ID then Web eID fallbacks." / "A blocked public demo or contract/payment requirement is a stop/replan finding."
revised: "The original spike prints subject fields and offers Mobile-ID, then Web eID, as fallbacks." / "If the public demo is blocked, or access requires a contract or payment, stop and replan."
rationale: Fixes the verb mismatch ("says print") and rewrites the noun stack as a condition and an action.

original: "Notification may be measured as fallback without changing the product wedge."
revised: Consider: "Notification mode may be measured as a fallback without changing the product's primary method (device link)?"
rationale: "wedge" is jargon with no definition. Check that "device link" is what the author means.

original: "Public subject exposes linkability" … "Pairwise default is a proposed privacy choice to confirm, not an approved source default."
revised: "A public `sub` value lets clients link one user across services." … "Making pairwise the default is a proposed privacy choice that still needs confirmation; the source does not approve it as the default."
rationale: Says who can link users and how. Replaces the noun stack "Pairwise default".

original: "A source logger warning that DEBUG may contain PII does not permit raw identifiers; typed no-PII logging first, sink masking as backstop at all levels."
revised: "A source logger warning that DEBUG may contain PII does not permit logging raw identifiers. Use typed no-PII logging as the primary control and sink masking as a backstop at every log level."
rationale: Completes the verb ("permit logging"). Turns the fragment into an instruction.

original: "Single-replica/process restart loses pending flows; retry fresh and document this instead of claiming HA."
revised: "Restarting the single replica or process loses pending flows, and users must start a new flow. Document this instead of claiming high availability."
rationale: "retry fresh" has no subject. Expands HA in place because it appears only once.

original: "Signing keys/trust files/config and synthetic fixtures are not retention of user flow history." / "demo named volume stores only that key"
revised: "Storing signing keys, trust files, configuration, and synthetic fixtures does not count as retaining user flow history." / "the demo's named volume stores only that key"
rationale: Replaces the slash chain and fixes the category error (keys "are not retention"). Adds the missing possessive.

original: "It does not make a passing hardened deployment claim." / "Default demo warning/banner repeats per source, without personal data."
revised: "A deployment that uses it cannot claim to be hardened." / Consider: "The demo warning banner is shown by default, as the source specifies, and contains no personal data?"
rationale: The first sentence misparses as written. In the second, "repeats" could mean "on every page" or "as the source says", so the author should check the intended meaning.

original: "Official permissive code can be reused with notice; no LGPL demo or unlicensed documentation copying."
revised: "Official permissively licensed code can be reused with attribution. Do not copy the LGPL demo or unlicensed documentation."
rationale: "no LGPL demo" can be read as "do not ship a demo". The intended rule is about copying.

original: "Prefer an appropriate maintained provider library over handwritten JWT/protocol mechanics, but do not invent a selection."
revised: "Prefer a maintained provider library over handwritten JWT and protocol code, but do not name one until the evaluation below is done."
rationale: "invent a selection" is unclear. "appropriate" adds nothing.

original: "Failure cannot be hidden by labelling omitted source AC done."
revised: "Do not hide a failure by marking omitted source acceptance criteria as done."
rationale: Turns the passive into a direct rule and expands AC.

original: "Access tokens for userinfo need an explicit bounded lifecycle: proposal is short-lived signed JWTs … unless explicitly necessary/allow-listed."
revised: "…: the proposal is short-lived signed JWTs … unless it is necessary and explicitly allow-listed."
rationale: Adds the missing article. "necessary/allow-listed" leaves open whether one condition or both is required. Check that "and" is right.

original: "Conformance harness after verified wallet method, core positive plus at least ten negative cases, pinned spec references and JUnit, no certification claim."
revised: "Build the conformance harness after the wallet method is verified. It covers the core positive case and at least ten negative cases, uses pinned spec references, and emits JUnit results. It makes no certification claim."
rationale: The fragment does not parse. The revision adds the verb and the relationships.

original: "Support source policy: latest minor fixes; pin/CA fixes backported one minor if maintained."
revised: Consider: "Support policy (from source): fixes ship in the latest minor release; pin and CA fixes are backported to the previous minor release while it is maintained?"
rationale: "latest minor fixes" and "one minor" are too compressed to read. Check the meaning.

original: "Private-key rotation/compromise recovery must be exercised." / "HTTP/request sizes"
revised: "Private-key rotation and compromise recovery must both be exercised." / Consider: "HTTP header and request body sizes?"
rationale: These slashes are ambiguous: "rotation/compromise" could mean "rotation or recovery". The guide says not to use a slash for "and/or". Other slash pairs in the document ("provisioning/linking", "templates/loggers/metrics", "built/tested", "short-lived/non-identifying") should become "and" or "or" in the same way.

original: "licence" (ADR-004, ADR-006), "license" (ADR-004 "hash/license metadata"), "labelling" (ADR-005); "80–100 hours" vs "80–100h"
revised: "license", "labeling"; "80–100 hours" everywhere
rationale: The document mixes British and US spelling inside one ADR. The Microsoft style guide uses US spelling and says to spell out units in prose.

original: Serial comma left out throughout, for example "client_secret_basic, client_secret_post and private_key_jwt", "hosted deployment or project-author data collection", "signature, root chain, validity, usage, certificate level and identity match"
revised: Add the serial comma: "…, client_secret_post, and private_key_jwt"
rationale: The Microsoft style guide requires the serial comma. It also removes ambiguity in long technical lists.

original: Code identifiers in plain text: acr=demo, eid_env=demo, TLS_PINS=disabled, personal_code, client_secret_basic, private_key_jwt, testdata, oss_inventory, COMPLETE, "Verify coverage" (threat table)
revised: Format them as code: `acr=demo`, `TLS_PINS=disabled`, `personal_code`, `testdata`, `Verify`, and so on
rationale: The Microsoft style guide puts code elements in code style. This separates literal values from prose. Consider whether "Verify" in the threat table is a function name.

original: Closing caveat (merged into Status): "Apply actual implementation-specific security review before a production release. Planning/source coverage is not cryptographic review or evidence that any product test passes."
revised: "Complete a security review of the actual implementation before any production release. This planning document is neither a cryptographic review nor evidence that any product test passes."
rationale: "Apply … review" is the wrong verb. "Planning/source coverage" is unclear.

original: "Registry of methods is internal until multiple implementations justify stabilizing it. OIDC and web receive a registry/contract, not a direct import of each backend."
revised: "The method registry stays internal until several implementations justify stabilizing it. The OIDC and web packages receive the registry interface, not direct imports of each backend."
rationale: Adds missing articles and says that "OIDC and web" are packages. "registry/contract" is resolved as a single interface. Check that reading.
